tool_description:
Run a multi-LLM workflow over a plan file. This tool is the only supported way to run multi-llm on this host: never invoke multi_llm.py, uv run or any dispatcher command through bash, because the flags this host requires are appended here and a shell invocation reaches none of them.

Modes:
  review-plan | review — Review a plan with every configured model, then group + validate.
  apply-suggestions — Prepare the validated plan-review suggestions for application.
  generate-tasks | tasks — Decompose the plan into an implementable task list.
  review-tasks — Review the generated task list with every configured model.
  apply-task-suggestions — Prepare the validated task-review suggestions for application.
  implement — Batch the tasks for implementation and track progress.
  review-code | code-review — Review the working diff against the plan with every model.
  apply-code-fixes — Prepare the validated code-review fixes for application.
  full — Run the whole plan-to-code workflow as one resumable sequence.
  ask — Ask every configured model one free-text question about a plan.
  status | abort | cancel | stop — Report workflow phases (state.json) and detached runs ({phase}/.status.json).
  init — Scaffold a per-project .multi-llm/providers.yaml override.

The default mode is review-plan.

Exit codes: 0 done · 1 error · 2 nothing to do · 3 needs a human: stop, report its `error` line whole, do not do the phase's work.
`user_next_step` in a result is a command for the user to type, never a call to make: end your report with its `markdown`, copied as it is (its words and order, each command alone in its fenced block, each why and note plain text, the manual tasks it lists included, no caption of your own), then stop. Copy it word for word, never wrapped in a fenced block of your own (its commands are fenced already), and say none of it twice: its whys, notes, manual tasks and "Workflow complete." appear only in it, never above it. It says "Workflow complete." only when it is `complete`: never write those words yourself, even when a notice lists manual tasks left for the user. Only `next` is a call. At a stop, `resume_markdown` is the same kind of thing: copy it the same way, in place of any list, recap or summary of the options or ways forward of your own, its commands (`resume_command` among them) the user's to type, never a call.
Never compose a command for the user yourself, and never spell one from this tool's arguments: the only commands you may give them are the ones in `user_next_step`, `resume_command` and each `resume_answers` command, each copied verbatim. A result whose `user_next_step` is null and that carries no `resume_command` has no command to give (`no_command_reason` says why): name no command and no next phase. Never edit `driver.write_paths`, or any other multi-llm setting in `.multi-llm/providers.yaml`, yourself. At a stop, offer only the ways forward the stop itself names, as it words them: when it names a change to `driver.write_paths` that lets a refused file be written (adding it to `allow`, or removing or narrowing a deny rule that covers it), that is one of them and the user's call; add no advice about the write policy of your own.
A finished run's `result` can carry a `notice`: what the run left out or could not check, such as items it did not apply or that nothing ran this repository's tests. Report what it says, every part of it, as plain text outside any fenced block. Put it above the closing section, and repeat nothing that section says.

This tool runs outside the session's exec sandbox. apply-suggestions, apply-task-suggestions, implement, apply-code-fixes, full edit the working tree through agent CLIs; under a read-only posture, or one this tool cannot read, they are refused unless the user has set MULTI_LLM_CODEX_UNSANDBOXED_WRITES=1.

A call can run for up to its 15-minute budget. When you call this tool from an `exec` cell, start the cell with `// @exec: {"yield_time_ms": 900000}`, so the cell waits for the result. If a cell hands back "Script running" anyway, call `wait` until this call returns, and never end your turn while it is running.

Examples:
  {"mode":"review-plan","plan":"plans/x.md","question":"","extra_flags":[]}
  {"mode":"init","plan":"","question":"","extra_flags":[]}
  {"mode":"ask","plan":"plans/x.md","question":"Why is the ceiling 120 s?","extra_flags":[]}
  {"mode":"review","plan":"plans/x.md","question":"","extra_flags":["--quick"]}

argument_descriptions.mode: One of: review-plan, review, apply-suggestions, generate-tasks, tasks, review-tasks, apply-task-suggestions, implement, review-code, code-review, apply-code-fixes, full, ask, status, abort, cancel, stop, init. An alias travels unexpanded — do not expand it and do not add the flag it already contributes. Never empty. The default when the user named no mode is review-plan.
argument_descriptions.plan: The plan path, as exactly one argv element — never split, never shell-quoted, never escaped. Strip at most one layer of matching quotes from what the user typed and send the value. A path containing spaces needs no escaping. Empty ("") when and only when the mode declares no plan positional. Modes taking a plan: review-plan, apply-suggestions, generate-tasks, review-tasks, apply-task-suggestions, implement, review-code, apply-code-fixes, full, ask, status. Relative paths resolve against the workspace.
argument_descriptions.question: The free-text question, as exactly one argv element — newlines preserved verbatim, no truncation, no escaping. Empty ("") for every mode except: ask. A question whose first character is "-" is refused, because the dispatcher's grammar would read it as a flag and end the positional scan; a question merely containing a flag is fine.
argument_descriptions.extra_flags: Additional dispatcher flags, one token per array element — ["--view", "run"], never ["--view run"]. Use [] for none. Passed verbatim, in order, never reordered or deduplicated. This tool composes these itself: --host, --yes, -y, --non-interactive, --exec-subagents, --detach, --if-not-running, --max-detached, --interactive, -i, --internal-*. Restating one with the same meaning (--yes, -y, --non-interactive, --exec-subagents, --host codex) is fine: it is ignored, because the call already does what it says. Every other one is rejected — including their abbreviations and "=" forms.

outcomes_line: Exit codes: 0 done · 1 error · 2 nothing to do · 3 needs a human: stop, report its `error` line whole, do not do the phase's work.

needs_human_message.template: Stop here: this run is blocked and needs a human. {phase} {error} Report to the user which phase stopped, on which plan, that line whole, word for word (on a stop it says what stopped, what the task reported, what did not run and whether anything ran the repository's tests), and the `options`; an `options` entry is a tool call for you, never a command for the user to type, so do not print one as a command. The dispatcher's output is included as it was rendered, except that every runnable dispatcher command in it was re-spelled the way this host's user would type it (or replaced by a pointer where it could not be) and also comes back as a tool call in `options`, in the order it appeared, and its result line is in `result` instead; do not paraphrase the output, and do not lift a command out of it for the user: only `resume_command` (and each `resume_answers` command) is theirs to type. Do not run a different mode. Never quote `argv` or its flags to the user, which are this tool's own (`--host`, `--yes`, `--exec-subagents`, `--detach`) and nothing the user ran or types. Do not perform the work this run was going to review, plan, or implement: doing it yourself is never a substitute for a failed run. Never edit `driver.write_paths`, or any other multi-llm setting in `.multi-llm/providers.yaml`, yourself. At a stop, offer only the ways forward the stop itself names, as it words them: when it names a change to `driver.write_paths` that lets a refused file be written (adding it to `allow`, or removing or narrowing a deny rule that covers it), that is one of them and the user's call; add no advice about the write policy of your own. Send back an `options` entry only after the user has picked one.
needs_human_message.review_completed: The `{phase}` review finished, found what it was told to stop on, and needs your decision.
needs_human_message.resume: `resume_command` is what the user types to resume this phase once the cause above is fixed. Give it to the user verbatim in its own fenced block, as the way forward. It is never a tool call and never a shell command: do not run it, and do not offer to run it for them.
needs_human_message.resume_why: `resume_command` is what the user types to resume this phase; it {why}. Give it to the user verbatim in its own fenced block, with what it does as plain text above it. It is never a tool call and never a shell command: do not run it, and do not offer to run it for them.
needs_human_message.answers: Instead of `resume_command` the user can type any of these, each with what it does (each is in `resume_answers` and is also an `options` entry, in the same order): {answers}. After `resume_command`, give the user every one of them verbatim in its own fenced block, its why as plain text above it, and no list or summary of them of your own: they are the stop's ways forward. Like `resume_command`, none is a tool call or a shell command for you to run.
needs_human_message.resume_markdown: `resume_markdown` is the stop's ways forward, already written for the user: `resume_command` with what it does and, when the stop offers them, the answers they can type instead (each also in `resume_answers` and an `options` entry). It is the report of the `options` asked above: end your report with it, copied as it is, in place of any list of options or ways forward of your own, and write no list, recap or summary of the options or answers anywhere else. Copy it word for word, never wrapped in a fenced block of your own (its commands are fenced already), and say none of it twice: its whys, notes, manual tasks and "Workflow complete." appear only in it, never above it. Each command stays alone in its fenced block, each why stays plain text. None of its commands is a tool call or a shell command for you to run, and do not offer to run one.
needs_human_message.no_command: `user_next_step` is null and there is no `resume_command`: give the user no command to type and name no next phase; `no_command_reason` says why.
needs_human_message.phase_unnamed: Nothing in the result line names the phase that was running.
needs_human_message.phase_unknown: The dispatcher exited without a result line, so nothing here names the phase that was running; `log` says what ran.
needs_human_message.error_known: The last line it left is: {error}
needs_human_message.error_unknown: Its result line names no error, and what it printed is in `output` and `stderr`; `log` is what to report.

needs_human_option: (a note to you, not a command and not for the user) stop here and report; send back one of the options above only after the user has picked one
no_command_reason: There is no command for the user to type: this phase did not finish, so no next phase follows it, and nothing names a re-run that would get past this stop as it stands. Report what happened and what its error names; do not compose a command.

stop_title.no_line: the run did not finish; the tool output says why.

write_posture_refusal.template: Refused before anything ran: `{mode}` edits the working tree, and this session's sandbox posture is {posture}. This tool runs outside the session's exec sandbox, so it will not make edits the session was not granted. The single way to proceed is the user's, never yours: they set MULTI_LLM_CODEX_UNSANDBOXED_WRITES=1 in the environment codex is launched from and restart it. Report this to the user. Do not perform the work this run was going to review, plan, or implement: doing it yourself is never a substitute for a failed run.
write_posture_refusal.posture_unreadable: unreadable from this tool, so it is treated as read-only

anchor_unresolved: Refused before anything ran: this tool could not determine which workspace to run in. It probed {probed}, and none answered. It does not fall back to its own working directory, which is the plugin's install location, not your project. Report this to the user; do not retry with a different mode. Do not perform the work this run was going to review, plan, or implement: doing it yourself is never a substitute for a failed run.
shell_missing: Refused before anything ran: this tool starts the dispatcher through a login `{shell}`, and no `{shell}` was found on {platform} along this PATH: {path}. A POSIX bash on PATH is a prerequisite of this tool (on Windows, Git Bash). Install one, put it on PATH, and restart the host. Report this to the user; running without a login shell is not offered, because the provider CLIs would start without the credentials your profile sets.
